items.review_rationale: Read the exact simple-root lifting condition: a root of the reduced monic polynomial mod maximal ideal lifts to R with the same residue. A simple root is not an arbitrary zero and polynomial monicity is a substantive hypothesis.

references.context: Commutative algebra: residue field of a local ring as quotient by the maximal ideal
Polynomial algebra: polynomial in one indeterminate with leading coefficient equal to 1

references.phrase: simple zero of reduced polynomial f-bar over κ
references.context: Polynomial algebra: simple root of the coefficientwise reduction of f modulo m

references.phrase: lifting a residue field root to R
references.context: Henselian algebra: element a∈R reducing modulo m to a-bar and satisfying f(a)=0

references.phrase: every monic polynomial and every simple zero
references.disposition: The quantifiers range over all eligible pairs; multiple roots in κ are not covered by this simple-root criterion.

items.review_rationale: Read the strict Henselian criterion as Henselianity plus a separably closed residue field, not an algebraically closed residue field: purely inseparable extensions may remain.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient κ=R/m by the maximal ideal of a local ring
Field theory: field with no nontrivial separable algebraic extensions, distinct from algebraically closed in positive characteristic

references.disposition: This does not require absence of nontrivial purely inseparable algebraic extensions.

items.review_rationale: Read the condition that S be a localization of some finitely presented R-algebra A, with finitely many polynomial generators and defining relations. It is stronger than essentially finite type but permits localization after presentation.

references.context: Commutative algebra: presentation A=R[T_1,…,T_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) with finite n and m

references.disposition: A may be chosen; S itself need not be finitely presented over R after arbitrary localization.

items.review_rationale: Read the existence of a finitely generated R-algebra A with a localization T^{-1}A isomorphic to S. Finite type refers to generators of A and does not assert a finite relation presentation.

references.context: Commutative algebra: bijective R-algebra map compatible with structural ring homomorphism

references.disposition: A is finite type over R, whereas S is only required to be isomorphic to its localization.

items.review_rationale: Read the descending-chain condition on ideals as the defining Artinian property for a commutative ring. Not the ascending-chain condition for Noetherian rings, and not finite cardinality of R.

references.context: Order theory: every decreasing sequence of ideals under inclusion eventually stabilizes

references.disposition: Every chain has its own stabilization index; Artinian does not mean the ring has a finite number of ideals.

items.review_rationale: Read the exact module-theoretic depth relative to ideal I as a supremum of lengths of M-regular sequences in I when IM differs from M; preserve the explicitly assigned infinite value when IM=M.

references.phrase: submodule IM generated by products I·M
references.context: Module theory: submodule generated by ideal coefficients multiplying elements of M

references.phrase: supremum of lengths of regular sequences
references.context: Order theory and commutative algebra: least upper bound or infinity for lengths of M-regular sequences in I

references.disposition: This is an explicit special convention; no regular sequence maximum is sought when IM=M.

items.review_rationale: Read local-ring depth as depth_m(M) for a finite module, using regular sequences from the maximal ideal; retain depth(0)=infinity convention rather than assuming nonzero module.

references.disposition: The zero module is explicitly assigned infinite depth; do not replace this with ordinary numerical sequence length.

items.review_rationale: Read the R-lattice condition in a finite-dimensional K-vector space over the fraction field of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain. The finite R-submodule must span V after scalar extension, not merely be any discrete lattice in a Euclidean space.

references.phrase: integral domain R and fraction field K
K-span of R-submodule M equals V
references.context: Linear algebra: linear span of M in a vector space over fraction field K

references.disposition: Dimension refers to Krull dimension of R, not to vector space dimension of V, which may be any finite value.
